To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a probabilistic representation of the task structure can be integrated with sensing information to allow a robot to anticipate human actions in collaborative assembly.
a robot can anticipate human actions for collaboration by probabilistic inference in the presence of uncertainty in both task and sensing.

(1) a representation is developed that allows the robot to probabilistically determine which task a human is performing and to predict the human's future actions; (2) the representation is used to develop an inference model that supports a planning and execution framework; and (3) this system enables a robot to anticipate human actions in the presence uncertain sensing and task ambiguities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods to allow robots to collaborate effectively with humans.
the development of a probabilistic model of human activity that allows a robot collaborator to anticipate the human's next action.
the problem of how to anticipate human actions in the context of collaborative tasks and how to do this in the presence of sensor uncertainty and task ambiguity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system can robustly anticipate future human actions in the presence both of task uncertainty and sensor uncertainty.
the robot is able to anticipate the future actions of a human in the context of an assembly task.
the system can robustly anticipate human actions for collaboration even in the presence task uncertainty and sensor noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a representation for structured activities that allows a robot, to probabilistically infer, which task actions a person is currently performing and predict which future actions the human is going to execute and when they will be executed.
we have developed a theory that allows a robot, in the presence of noisy and unreliable sensing, to anticipate what the human is doing and to plan accordingly.
we have shown a method for a robot to anticipate human actions in the presence task and sensor uncertainty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a probabilistic model can be developed for a robot to anticipate human actions in a collaborative task even when the robot has incomplete knowledge about the task and sensing is uncertain.
we show how to integrate sensing and task structure in a way that allows the robot to anticipate human actions even when sensing is noisy and task structure is ambiguous.
a robot can anticipate human actions in an uncertain world and can use that anticipation to minimize human idle time and improve human-robot interaction.
